questions.q: Why does this lesson focus on diagram content rather than any particular diagramming tool?
options: A diagram is only as good as the content decisions behind it — what to include, what to leave out, and what question it lets a reviewer answer at a glance
ServiceNow does not allow architecture diagrams to be created in any external tool
This course requires every diagram to be built in a specific named tool
Diagram content is irrelevant as long as the diagram looks professional
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates the drawing tool from the actual skill being taught: deciding what content the diagram needs to carry.

questions.q: What two questions should a reviewer be able to answer at a glance from Meridian's instance/domain topology diagram?
options: Which vendor originally sold ServiceNow to Meridian
How many total employees work at each hospital system
Whether a Lakeshore agent can see a St. Catherine's incident, and whether a Meridian executive can see across all three domains for board reporting
What color scheme the ServiceNow portal uses at each hospital system
questions.explain: The lesson states that if the topology diagram can't answer these two domain-visibility questions at a glance, it isn't doing its job yet.

questions.q: Why does the integration data-flow diagram need to show which domain each integration's resulting record lands in?
options: ServiceNow requires every diagram to list a domain regardless of relevance
This detail is purely cosmetic and makes the diagram easier to color-code
So a reviewer can catch, on paper, any integration path that doesn't correctly assign a sys_domain value before it's built
The resulting domain has no real bearing on whether the integration works correctly
questions.explain: Tracing where each record's domain gets assigned is what makes the diagram catch a real design flaw before implementation, not just illustrate a flow.

questions.q: In the ADR for the single-instance-with-domain-separation decision, why does the lesson insist on stating why Options A and B were rejected, not just that Option C was chosen?
options: Rejected options are required by ServiceNow's platform for compliance reasons
Listing rejected options is optional padding with no real value
An ADR is only valid if it lists at least five rejected options
Recording the rejected alternatives and the reasoning against them is what lets a future reader judge whether the original constraints still hold, per Chapter 1's ADR discipline
questions.explain: This reuses Chapter 1's point directly: the rejected options and reasoning are often the most valuable part of the record for a future reader.

questions.q: What does the ADR's 'consequences' section honestly state about the domain-separation decision?
options: The decision eliminates the need for any future security review
There are no real downsides to the domain-separation decision
Domain separation makes every future development task faster with no added complexity
Every future script, report, and integration on the instance now has to be built and tested with domain awareness — a permanent cost accepted deliberately
questions.explain: The lesson insists the ADR state the real, ongoing cost honestly, not just the benefits of the chosen option.
